metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Arona, PA | Westmoreland Co.
metaDescription: Arona, PA mineral owners: get a straightforward cash offer on your Marcellus interest in Westmoreland County, no obligation to accept.
heroLead: Arona is a small borough tucked between larger Westmoreland County towns, and most of the mineral ownership around it is still farm-family land.
intro: You won't find a lot written about Arona specifically, but the farmland surrounding it has been part of Westmoreland County's steady, if less flashy, Marcellus development for over a decade. Owners here tend to hold modest acreage passed down through a family that worked the land long before any gas company came calling, and the royalty income, when it exists, has usually been a quiet supplement rather than a windfall.
We approach every conversation the same way we'd want someone to approach ours: explain the paperwork first, then talk numbers.

sections.heading: Modest acreage, real participation
paragraphs: A small tract near Arona can still be pooled into a spacing unit alongside larger neighboring properties, which means your royalty share reflects the whole unit's production rather than just what's directly under your family's land. That's standard practice under Pennsylvania's oil and gas conservation law, but it's rarely explained clearly when the original lease gets signed.
This part of the county is generally within the wet-gas Marcellus window, so expect a processing-related deduction on your statement in addition to normal well decline.

sections.heading: What we do before quoting a price
paragraphs: We trace your interest through the Westmoreland County Recorder of Deeds, confirm your net mineral acreage, and check whether your tract is currently leased, held by production, or open. If there's a gap in the paperwork, we tell you what's missing instead of leaving it as a mystery.

sections.heading: Why a small interest is still worth evaluating
paragraphs: Even a modest fractional interest can add up to a meaningful lump sum once you're no longer waiting on a quarterly check that barely moves the needle. We evaluate interests of nearly any size and give you an honest answer either way.

faqs.question: My acreage near Arona is small. Is it even worth calling about?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Send what you have, even if it's a small fractional interest, and we'll give you a straightforward answer.

faqs.question: How do you know if my land is part of a producing unit?
faqs.answer: We check state well and unit records against your parcel to confirm, and explain what we find before making an offer.

faqs.question: Will you come out to look at the property?
faqs.answer: Usually not necessary. Mineral evaluations are done through title, lease, and production records rather than a physical site visit.
